title: Kicker Candle
teaches: The Kicker as we trade it: a leader already set up, a real red day that closes weak at support, then a day that gaps up at least 1.5%, trades through the red day's high and never fills the gap; the buy is a market order over the red high on the Kicker day (never the close), the stop a few cents under the Kicker day's low or 3.5% under the entry if closer, a third off at 3R and 5R, and a stop-out is the plan working.

walkthroughs.title: BBY, July 2013: the cleanest two candles on a base
steps: BBY, 2013. A leader coils in a 6.2% range. The red day, down 1.8%, closes at 2% of its range.
Sellers think it is breaking down. Next morning it gaps up 2.1% over that close, and the gap holds.
2013-07-01: it trades through the red high. Buy at market, 27.97. Stop a few cents under the low so far, 3.5% max.
The gap holds: it closes at 92% of its range, up 8.8%. On the scan's stop, 3R came in a day.

walkthroughs.title: COHR, January 2024: a fill at the open
steps: COHR, 2024. A six-week shelf on the 21-day EMA. The red day, down 1.8%, closes at 19% of its range.
2024-01-16: it gaps up 2.6% and opens just over the red high, 42.83. A market order fills at the open.
No low yet: the first stop is 3.5% under the fill, 41.33. At 10:00 raise it to the 30-minute low if higher.
Failure mode: the gap fills. Instead it closes at 81% of its range, up 8.2%. 3R takes four days: a third off.

walkthroughs.title: ATRO, June 2026: the trims and the trail
steps: ATRO, 2026. The red day, down 2.7%, drops into the 21-day EMA and the 50-day. It closes at 13% of its range.

A doji, then a small inside day
Two red days that each gap down
questions.answer: Weak red day, then a gap over its high
questions.why: Weak red day, then a gap over its high. The red day looks like a breakdown at support. The gap up traps the sellers.
questions.lesson_line: A Kicker is a failed breakdown followed by a gap that traps the sellers.

wrong.Green day, then a red day under its low: That is a drop after strength. A Kicker is a red day, then a gap up.
wrong.A doji, then a small inside day: A doji or a baby candle traps nobody, and an inside day has no gap.
wrong.Two red days that each gap down: Gaps down are the opposite. The Kicker day gaps up.

questions.q: A Kicker can follow a baby red candle or a doji.
questions.why: False. A baby red candle or a doji is not the red day. Nobody is trapped, so a gap after one is just a breakout.
questions.lesson_line: No trapped sellers, no kick. After a baby candle it is a plain breakout.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The Kicker day opens at least ___% above the red day's close.
questions.why: 1.5%. The gap is measured from the red day's close. A smaller gap is a plain breakout day.
questions.lesson_line: A Kicker gap is at least 1.5% over the red day's close.

questions.q: On the Kicker day, where is the buy trigger?
choices: One cent over the red day's high
The Kicker day's close, at market
One cent under the red day's low
A cent over the red day's open
questions.answer: One cent over the red day's high
questions.why: One cent over the red day's high. Buy at market as it trades through, on the Kicker day only.
questions.lesson_line: The trigger is the trade through the red high. The close is too late.

wrong.The Kicker day's close, at market: Buying the close is a named mistake. The entry is the trade through the red high.
wrong.One cent under the red day's low: The low is where the sellers were trapped, not where we buy.
wrong.A cent over the red day's open: The open of the red day is not a level in this plan. The red high is the trigger.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The buy over the red high is a market order on the ___ day only.
questions.why: Kicker. The buy is on the Kicker day only. The next day is too late for this trigger.
questions.lesson_line: The red-high trigger works on the Kicker day only.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The Kicker stop sits a few cents under the Kicker day's ___.
questions.why: Low. The stop sits a few cents under the Kicker day's low, or 3.5% under the entry if that is closer.
questions.lesson_line: Stop under the Kicker day's low, or 3.5% under the entry if that is closer.

questions.q: A Red market is no place for a Kicker.
questions.why: True. The reading must be Green or Yellow, with Orange only for an A+. In Red it is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Check the market first. In a Red market the Kicker waits.

questions.q: What does 'the gap holds' mean on the Kicker day?
choices: It stays over the red day's close
It closes above its open on volume
It opens over the red day's high
It stays above the 50-day all day
questions.answer: It stays over the red day's close
questions.why: It never trades back to the red close. If it does, the gap has filled and the Kicker is off.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that fills is not a Kicker. Hold above the red close or walk away.

wrong.It closes above its open on volume: The test is the red close, not the open. A gap can hold on a day that fades.
wrong.It opens over the red day's high: That is where it opens, not what holds. The gap holds if it never trades back to the red close.
wrong.It stays above the 50-day all day: The 50-day is context before the red day. The gap holds against the red close.

questions.q: Where does a Kicker belong?
choices: On a base or an orderly pullback
After a vertical run with no base
Under a falling 200-day
On any earnings gap
questions.answer: On a base or an orderly pullback
questions.why: On a base or an orderly pullback. The leader is already set up above its 200-day, and the red day shakes it.
questions.lesson_line: No base, no setup. The Kicker sits on top of a leader that is already set up.

wrong.After a vertical run with no base: The last 20 closes must span 15% or less. A stock mid-run has no base.
wrong.Under a falling 200-day: No longs below the 200-day, except a parabolic long.
wrong.On any earnings gap: The first session after a report is mostly an earnings gapper, a PEG.

questions.q: The textbook kicking pattern is a bearish candle, a gap up, then a bullish candle.
questions.why: True. Bulkowski and Schwab agree on that order, and Schwab adds that neither candle has shadows. Ours is looser.
questions.lesson_line: Textbook kicking is shadowless. Ours is a real red day, a gap and context.

questions.q: What is the Kicker stop cap?
choices: 3.5% under the entry price
3% under the entry price
7% under the entry price
The base low
questions.why: 3.5% under the entry price. The Kicker keeps its own cap, not the usual 3%. Over 3.5% is not a clean Kicker.
questions.lesson_line: The Kicker cap is 3.5%. A wider honest stop means pass.

wrong.3% under the entry price: That is the usual rule of thumb for stops. The Kicker keeps 3.5%.
wrong.7% under the entry price: That is twice the cap. A stop that wide means it is not a clean Kicker.
wrong.The base low: The base low can be far away. The stop sits under the Kicker day.

questions.q: A Kicker is about positioning and is rarely an earnings gap.
questions.why: True. The first session after a report is mostly an earnings gapper, a Power Earnings Gap.
questions.lesson_line: Kickers are positioning. The day after a report belongs to the earnings gapper.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Before the red day, the last 20 closes span ___% or less.
questions.why: 15%. A base or an orderly pullback is tight. A stock mid-run with no base is not a setup.
questions.lesson_line: Twenty closes inside a 15% span: that is the base under the red day.

questions.q: Where should the red day end?
choices: At support, like the 21 or 50-day
In open air, well above the highs
At a fresh 52-week high on volume
Anywhere, as long as it is red
questions.why: At support, like the 21-day or 50-day. A drop into a level traps the sellers who sold the break.
questions.lesson_line: The red day falls into a level. That is what makes the gap a trap.

wrong.In open air, well above the highs: There is no level to fail at. The red day closes at support.
wrong.At a fresh 52-week high on volume: That is no breakdown at support. The red day ends at a level.
wrong.Anywhere, as long as it is red: A red day in the middle of nowhere traps nobody. It must fall into a level.

questions.q: After you buy a Kicker, a bearish engulfing candle is not a reason to sell before the stop.
questions.why: True. No early exit on a gap back, a bearish engulfing candle or a close under the red high. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A candle is not an exit. The stop is.

questions.q: What floor must a Kicker stock clear?
choices: $10 a share and $20 million a day
$5 a share and $5 million a day
$2 a share and $10,000 a day
No floor for leaders
questions.answer: $10 a share and $20 million a day
questions.why: $10 a share and $20 million a day. Thin stocks are not even watched.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars a share, twenty million a day. Below that, no Kicker.

wrong.$5 a share and $5 million a day: Too low. Our floor is $10 a share and $20 million a day.
wrong.$2 a share and $10,000 a day: That is the app detector floor, far under ours. Our floor is $10 and $20 million.
wrong.No floor for leaders: Every setup has the floor. Illiquid stocks are not even watched.

questions.q: If the 3.5% stop is too wide for your risk, tighten the stop until the size fits.
questions.why: False. Size comes from the stop. If the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
questions.lesson_line: Never fit the stop to the size. Fit the size to the stop, or skip.

questions.q: How much comes off at the first trim, 3R?
choices: A third
Half
All of it
A quarter
questions.why: A third. The hard rule is a third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the rest.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, and trail the last third.

wrong.Half: The hard rule is a third, not half.
wrong.All of it: Trims are thirds. The last third is trailed.
wrong.A quarter: The hard rule is a third at 3R.

questions.q: You may own 5% of a stock's average daily volume if the Kicker is clean.
questions.why: False. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. Illiquid stocks are not even watched.
questions.lesson_line: Size to the stock too. One percent of its daily volume is the ceiling.

questions.q: Bought at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 23.40. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. This is the MS trade, 3R in 2 days.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Which red day sets up the better Kicker?
choices: It closes near its low, into the 21-day
It closes mid-range after a lazy drift
It closes near its high on a small range
questions.answer: It closes near its low, into the 21-day
questions.why: It closes near its low, into the 21-day. A weak close at support looks like a breakdown. A mid-range close does not.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close at support sets the trap. A mid-range close is a regular gap up.

wrong.It closes mid-range after a lazy drift: A mid-range close traps fewer sellers. It grades lower, and it is often just a regular gap up.
wrong.It closes near its high on a small range: A strong close traps nobody. The red day must close weak.

questions.q: A Kicker can also be bought on a break of the first 30-minute high on day one.
questions.why: True. Entry B is one cent over the high of the first 30-minute bar of the Kicker day.
questions.lesson_line: Two entries: over the red high, or over the first 30-minute high.

questions.q: The red day closed at 44.10. The Kicker day opens at 44.75. How big is the gap, in percent?
questions.why: 1.47%. That is short of the 1.5% line, so there is no Kicker gap. Round it and it looks closer than it is.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap. A gap a hair short of the line is not a gap.

questions.q: Where is the buy?
choices: 27.97, a cent over the red high
28.50, a round number above it
The Kicker day's close at market
27.60, just under the red low
questions.story: The red day's high is 27.96. The next morning the stock gaps up 2.1% but opens under that high, then trades up through it.
questions.answer: 27.97, a cent over the red high
questions.why: 27.97. The buy is one cent over the red day's high, as it trades through. That is how BBY was bought on 2013-07-01.
questions.lesson_line: Buy one cent over the red high as it trades through.

wrong.28.50, a round number above it: You buy as it trades through the red high, not at a round number above it.
wrong.The Kicker day's close at market: Never at the close. The trigger is the trade through the red high.
wrong.27.60, just under the red low: That is a buy below the trigger, before the gap has proved itself.

questions.q: Where does your first stop go?
choices: 40.53, 3.5% under the fill
41.85, just under the red high
No stop until 10:00, then 3.5%
Under the red day's low
questions.story: The red high was 41.90. The Kicker day opens over it, and you are filled at the open at 42.00. The day has no low yet.
questions.why: 40.53. An open fill has no Kicker low yet, so the first stop is 3.5% under the fill. It is a real stop with the broker.
questions.lesson_line: No low yet means 3.5% under the fill. Raise it once the low exists.

wrong.41.85, just under the red high: The red high is the trigger. The first stop on an open fill is the 3.5% cap.
wrong.No stop until 10:00, then 3.5%: Every position has a real stop order from the start. At 10:00 it only moves up.
wrong.Under the red day's low: The stop sits under the Kicker day, not the red day.

questions.q: Filled at 27.98. The Kicker day's low so far is 26.90. Where is the stop?
questions.why: 27.00. The stop is a few cents under the low or 3.5% under the entry, whichever is closer. 3.5% under the fill is closer.
questions.lesson_line: Two stops, one answer: take the one closer to the entry.

questions.q: The buy point is 83.20. The Kicker opens at 86.00. How far above the buy point is that, in percent?
questions.why: 3.4%. That is inside the 4% chase limit, so the open is still a buy. Past 4% it is not.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the open against your buy point. Up to 4% is fine, past it is chasing.

questions.q: Can you buy the open?
choices: No; over 4% above the buy point
Yes, a gap up shows strength
Yes, with a smaller stop to fit
Yes, but only at half size
questions.story: The red high is 50.00, so your buy point is 50.01. The Kicker day opens at 52.60.
questions.answer: No; over 4% above the buy point
questions.why: No. The open is more than 4% above the buy point. We never chase; chasing costs size, because the stop stays put.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the buy point, the open is not ours.

wrong.Yes, a gap up shows strength: Strength is not a reason to chase. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
wrong.Yes, with a smaller stop to fit: You do not tighten the stop to fit. The stop stays put and the distance grows.
wrong.Yes, but only at half size: Half size does not change the rule. No buy more than 4% above the buy point.

questions.q: Which of these ends the trade before you buy?
choices: It trades back to the red close
It gaps up 2.4% on heavy volume
It trades over the red day's high
questions.answer: It trades back to the red close
questions.why: It trades back to the red day's close. The gap has filled before the trigger, so there is no trade.
questions.lesson_line: A filled gap is a dead Kicker. Walk away.

wrong.It gaps up 2.4% on heavy volume: A gap of 1.5% or more is what you want. A filled gap is what kills it.

questions.q: Do you buy it?
choices: No, a report is inside 3 sessions
Yes, it is a Kicker, not earnings
Yes, at half size
Yes, then sell before the report
questions.story: A clean Kicker triggers over the red high. The company reports earnings in two sessions.
questions.answer: No, a report is inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before a report. A report this close can gap the stock past your stop.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.Yes, it is a Kicker, not earnings: The report window is its own rule and the Kicker does not escape it.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change the rule. No new buys within 3 days.
wrong.Yes, then sell before the report: The rule is no new buys inside the window, not buy and run.

questions.q: What do you do with the stop?
choices: Raise it a few cents under 41.30
Leave it, a stop never changes
Move it to breakeven at 10:00
Lower it to give it more room
questions.story: You were filled at the open at 42.00 with the stop at 40.53. It is 10:00 and the first 30-minute low is 41.30.
questions.answer: Raise it a few cents under 41.30
questions.why: Raise it. At 10:00 the stop moves to a few cents under the 30-minute low if that is higher. A stop only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: At 10:00 an open-fill stop moves up to the 30-minute low.

wrong.Leave it, a stop never changes: A stop only moves up, and this is the one moment it should.
wrong.Move it to breakeven at 10:00: Breakeven comes with the first trim, not at 10:00.
wrong.Lower it to give it more room: A stop never moves down or wider.

questions.q: Sell at the close, or hold?
choices: Hold; the stop is the exit
Sell at the close
Move the stop to breakeven
Add on the dip
questions.story: You bought the Kicker over the red high. At the close it sits back under that high, but above your stop.
questions.answer: Hold; the stop is the exit
questions.why: Hold. A close back under the red high is a warning for the grade, not an exit. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close is a warning. Only the stop sells you.

wrong.Sell at the close: No early exit on a close under the red high.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven: Breakeven comes with the first trim.
wrong.Add on the dip: We buy once, at one price with one stop.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
choices: 98.20, the first 30-minute low
100.00, where it was
Out at once, the loss is past 2R
The open, 98.50, the gap price
questions.story: You bought at 103.50 with the stop at 100.00. The next morning it gaps open at 98.50. The first 30-minute low is 98.20.
questions.why: 98.20. A gap down through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.100.00, where it was: The stop is already through. The 30-minute low is the new stop.
wrong.Out at once, the loss is past 2R: The loss at the 30-minute low is inside the 2R ceiling.
wrong.The open, 98.50, the gap price: The open is not the decision. The 30-minute low is.

questions.q: Do you buy the close?
choices: No, the trigger already passed
Yes, a strong close confirms it
Yes, at half size
Yes, with a 3.5% stop
questions.story: The Kicker day ran over the red high at 45.10 and closes strong at 47.20. You were away and did not buy.
questions.why: No. The entry is the trade through the red high, not the close. Buying the close is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Miss the trigger and you miss the trade. Do not buy the close.

wrong.Yes, a strong close confirms it: The close confirms the chart, but the buy was the trade through the high.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Smaller size does not fix a late entry.
wrong.Yes, with a 3.5% stop: The stop does not fix the entry. Never at the close.

questions.q: Fill 55.00. The 10-day average is 49.00. How far above the 10-day is the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 12.2%. That is more than 10% above the 10-day average, so we skip it.
questions.lesson_line: Too stretched to buy: skip a long more than 10% over its 10-day.

questions.q: The Kicker gap is measured from which price?
choices: The red day's close
The red day's open
The red day's high
The red day's low
questions.why: The red day's close. Bigalow measures from the prior open. Ours is the gap over the red close, at least 1.5%.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap from the red close, not the open.

wrong.The red day's open: That is Bigalow's version. Ours is the red close.
wrong.The red day's high: The red high is the trigger, not the start of the gap.
wrong.The red day's low: The low is not a gap reference.

questions.q: Filled at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 1.8%. Well inside the 3.5% cap, so the stop is honest and the Kicker is clean.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop. Inside 3.5% is a clean Kicker.

questions.q: Account 100,000, risk 0.5%. Fill 22.17, stop 21.76. How many shares, rounded down? The position cap does not bind.
questions.why: 1219 shares. Account times risk percent, divided by fill minus stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, then size. Shares are risk dollars over the stop distance.

questions.q: What do you do at 23.40?
choices: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
Sell it all and take the 3R
Sell half, keep the same stop
Hold all, nudge the stop up
questions.story: You bought at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. The Kicker reaches 23.40, which is 3R.
questions.answer: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third and move the stop to breakeven. 23.40 is 3R. The first trim is a third at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: At 3R sell a third and lift the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell it all and take the 3R: Trims are thirds, and the last third is trailed.
wrong.Sell half, keep the same stop: The hard rule is a third, and the stop moves up at the first trim.
wrong.Hold all, nudge the stop up: The first third comes off at 3R.

questions.q: When do you take the first trim?
choices: At the open, 24.10
At the close
When it falls back to 23.40
Wait for 5R
questions.story: Your Kicker's 3R level is 23.40. The next morning it opens at 24.10.
questions.why: At the open, 24.10. If a day opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Open past the level, take the trim at the open.

wrong.At the close: The rule is to take it at the open.
wrong.When it falls back to 23.40: You may never get that price back.
wrong.Wait for 5R: The first third comes off at 3R. The open is past it.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell it and free the money
Hold for 5R, the trend is up
Add on a breakout of the range
Widen the stop to give it room
questions.story: It is day 10. The Kicker has chopped sideways and sits at +0.6R. The stop has not been touched.
questions.answer: Sell it and free the money
questions.why: Sell it. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and under 1R: sell and use the money elsewhere.

wrong.Hold for 5R, the trend is up: A trade under 1R after 10 days is sold.
wrong.Add on a breakout of the range: We buy once, and a slow trade is not a reason to add.

questions.q: Do you add?
choices: No, we buy once
Yes, with the same stop
Yes, at half size
Yes, if it is up 1R
questions.story: The Kicker works. Two days later it pushes over the Kicker day's high on strong volume.
questions.why: No. One entry at one price with one stop. Adding on the next push is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: One entry, one stop, no adds.

wrong.Yes, with the same stop: No adds on the next push.

questions.q: On one stock you may try at most 3 times a week and 6 times a month.
questions.why: True. That is our limit on one stock. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.
questions.lesson_line: Stopped out means the next try needs a new trigger.

questions.q: Which average is the default trail for a fast mover?
choices: The 10-day
The 50-day
The 200-day
The 5-day
questions.why: The 10-day. Sell on a close below it. Steadier names trail the 21-day.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 10-day. Steadier name, 21-day. Sell on a close below.

wrong.The 50-day: Too slow for the default trail. The 10-day or the 21-day.
wrong.The 200-day: That is the long-term line, far too slow for a trail.
wrong.The 5-day: The defaults are the 10-day and the 21-day.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Take it only if it is an A+
Take it at full size
Pass, only Green allows it
Short the market instead
questions.story: A clean Kicker triggers, but the market reading is Orange.
questions.answer: Take it only if it is an A+
questions.why: Take it only as an A+. In an Orange market only A+ setups. Green is full risk, Yellow smaller and fewer.
questions.lesson_line: Orange market, A+ only. Yellow, smaller. Green, full.

wrong.Pass, only Green allows it: Orange allows an A+. Red is mostly cash.
wrong.Short the market instead: Red is mostly cash and shorts. Orange still allows an A+ long.

questions.q: An alert from the app that says Kicker is enough to buy.
questions.why: False. The raw alert fires on red, gap-filling days. Check every rule yourself before you buy.
questions.lesson_line: An alert is a lead, not a trade. Check the rules.

questions.q: Buy now?
choices: No, regular hours only
Yes, the gap is open
Yes, with a limit order
Yes, half now and half at 9:30
questions.story: At 8:30 in the pre-market the stock trades over the red high on a gap up.
questions.why: No. No new buys outside regular trading hours.
questions.lesson_line: The Kicker triggers in regular hours. Not pre-market.

wrong.Yes, the gap is open: The trigger counts in regular hours only.
wrong.Yes, with a limit order: Entries are market orders in regular hours.
wrong.Yes, half now and half at 9:30: No buys at all outside regular hours.

questions.q: What is it?
choices: Earnings gapper, graded as a PEG
A Kicker, the red day was weak
An episodic pivot in a neglected name
A Launchpad over the averages
questions.story: A weak red day, then a gap up 6.2% and a close up 18.7%. The company reported after the close the night before.
questions.answer: Earnings gapper, graded as a PEG
questions.why: An earnings gapper, graded as a PEG. The gap day is the earnings reaction day. That was LUV on 2026-01-29.
questions.lesson_line: The first session after a report is an earnings gapper, whatever the red day looked like.

wrong.A Kicker, the red day was weak: The first session after a report is mostly an earnings gapper, whatever the red day looked like.
wrong.An episodic pivot in a neglected name: An EP is a 10% gap in a neglected name. This gap sits on a report, so it is an earnings gapper.
wrong.A Launchpad over the averages: A Launchpad has no gap and a tight bundle of averages.

questions.q: Why is it not a Kicker?
choices: The gap is under 1.5%
It closed too strong
The red day fell too far
It broke the red high
questions.story: A red day closes at 7% of its range. The next day opens 0.8% over that close, trades through the red high and closes up 8.4%.
questions.why: The gap is under 1.5%. It opened 0.8% over the red close. That was CEG on 2024-06-10, a plain breakout day with no gap.
questions.lesson_line: A strong green bar without a 1.5% gap is a breakout, not a Kicker.

wrong.It closed too strong: A strong close is what a Kicker does.
wrong.The red day fell too far: The failing number is the gap, not the red day.
wrong.It broke the red high: Trading through the red high is the trigger.

questions.q: Kicker, or a plain breakout?
choices: A plain breakout, nobody was trapped
A Kicker, the gap is big enough
A Kicker, the base is tight
An episodic pivot
questions.story: The red day's body is 0.04% of price, and it fell 0.4%. The next day gaps 2.2%, trades through the high and closes up 5.8%, out of a 4.8% base.
questions.answer: A plain breakout, nobody was trapped
questions.why: A plain breakout. A baby red candle traps nobody, so there is no kick. That was GWW on 2024-10-11.
questions.lesson_line: A baby red candle before the gap makes it a breakout.

wrong.A Kicker, the gap is big enough: The gap is fine. The red day is a baby candle, so no sellers were trapped.
wrong.A Kicker, the base is tight: The base is fine. It fails on the red day.
wrong.An episodic pivot: An EP gaps 10% or more. This gap is 2.2%.

questions.q: Which rule fails?
choices: No base: the 20 closes span too much
The gap is too small for a Kicker
The red day closed too strong
The stop is over 3.5% of the entry
questions.story: The red day falls 5.8% and closes at 1% of its range. The next day gaps 5.7% and closes up 13.8%. The prior 20 closes span 44.1%.
questions.answer: No base: the 20 closes span too much
questions.why: No base. The prior 20 closes span 44.1%, far past 15%. That was IDCC on 2011-08-03, a stock mid-run. It was stopped the next day.
questions.lesson_line: No base, no Kicker. A stock mid-run is not set up.

wrong.The gap is too small for a Kicker: A gap of 5.7% is well past 1.5%.
wrong.The red day closed too strong: It closed at 1% of its range, a weak close.
wrong.The stop is over 3.5% of the entry: The failing rule is the base, not the stop.

questions.q: Kicker, or a red to green?
choices: A red to green, not a Kicker
A Kicker with a shakeout
An episodic pivot
questions.story: Yesterday was a weak red day. Today opens up 2%, dips under yesterday's close, then rallies back over it.
questions.answer: A red to green, not a Kicker
questions.why: A red to green. A red-to-green entry trades under the prior close first and then back over it. A Kicker never trades back to the red close.
questions.lesson_line: If it trades back to the red close, the gap filled. It is not a Kicker.

wrong.A Kicker with a shakeout: The gap holds on a Kicker. Trading back under the red close fills it.
wrong.An episodic pivot: An EP is a gap of 10% or more in a neglected name.

questions.q: Kicker, or a plain breakout?
choices: A plain breakout, the red day is a doji
A Kicker, the gap is the point
A Kicker, the base is tight
questions.story: Yesterday was a doji inside a tight base. Today gaps up through the top of the base.
questions.answer: A plain breakout, the red day is a doji
questions.why: A plain breakout. A doji is not the red day, so nobody was trapped.
questions.lesson_line: A doji in the base is not a red day. The gap makes it a breakout.

wrong.A Kicker, the gap is the point: The gap needs a real red day under it.
wrong.A Kicker, the base is tight: The base is fine, but the red day is a doji.

questions.q: Kicker, or an episodic pivot?
choices: An episodic pivot, not a Kicker
A Kicker, the red day was small
A Launchpad
questions.story: A neglected stock gaps up 12% on a named surprise and huge volume. The day before was a small red day.
questions.answer: An episodic pivot, not a Kicker
questions.why: An episodic pivot. An EP gaps 10% or more on huge volume in a neglected name. A Kicker is a smaller gap on a stock already set up.
questions.lesson_line: Size and surprise name the setup. A 12% gap on news is an EP.

wrong.A Kicker, the red day was small: A Kicker is a smaller gap on a stock already set up. This is a 12% surprise in a neglected name.
wrong.A Launchpad: A launch bar has no gap.

questions.q: Kicker, or a Launchpad?
choices: A Launchpad, there was no gap
A Kicker, it cleared the averages
An episodic pivot
questions.story: A stock closes above all four of its averages out of a tight bundle. It opens flat. The day before was a small green day.
questions.answer: A Launchpad, there was no gap
questions.why: A Launchpad. A launch bar closes above all four averages out of a tight bundle with no gap. A Kicker needs a weak red day and a gap.
questions.lesson_line: No gap and no red day means a launch bar, not a Kicker.

wrong.A Kicker, it cleared the averages: A Kicker needs a real red day yesterday and a gap of 1.5% or more.

questions.q: Does the context pass?
choices: No; the 50-day must be flat or up
Yes, a gap is strength enough
Yes, if the 200-day is rising
Yes, at half size
questions.story: A Kicker triggers cleanly, but the 50-day average has been falling for weeks.
questions.answer: No; the 50-day must be flat or up
questions.why: No. The context needs a flat or rising 50-day. A gap against a falling 50-day is a gap against the trend.
questions.lesson_line: Check the 50-day first. A Kicker needs a flat or rising one.

wrong.Yes, a gap is strength enough: The gap does not fix the trend. The 50-day must be flat or rising.
wrong.Yes, if the 200-day is rising: The 200-day is one line of context. The 50-day is another.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change the context.

questions.q: What was wrong with this one?
choices: A shock-day red bar is no pullback
The gap was too big to hold up
It closed too strong to trust
The stop was too tight for the day
questions.story: The red day fell 5.9% in a one-day market shock. The next day it gapped 8.7%, closed up 9.9%, then gave it all back.
questions.answer: A shock-day red bar is no pullback
questions.why: A shock-day red bar is not an orderly pullback. That was AVGO on 2025-10-13. It was stopped the next session.
questions.lesson_line: A one-day shock bar is not an orderly pullback.

wrong.The gap was too big to hold up: The gap was big but the shock day under it is the problem.
wrong.It closed too strong to trust: A strong close is the Kicker. The problem was the red day.
wrong.The stop was too tight for the day: The stop was the 3.5% cap, the widest we use.

questions.q: Do you take it?
choices: No, a Red market has no Kicker
Yes, the chart is textbook
Yes, at half size
Yes, with a tight stop
questions.story: A leader fell 10.0% on a red day, then gaps up 5.5% and closes up 10.6%. The whole market is in a crash and the reading is Red.
questions.answer: No, a Red market has no Kicker
questions.why: No. A bounce in a Red market looks like a Kicker and is not. That was LLY on 2020-03-13, stopped at 0R.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first. A bounce in a crash is not a Kicker.

wrong.Yes, the chart is textbook: The shape was textbook and still failed. In Red we are mostly cash.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change a Red market.
wrong.Yes, with a tight stop: A tight stop does not fix the market.

questions.q: Why would the rules have skipped it?
choices: A report was due inside 3 sessions
The gap was too big to be a Kicker
The stop was too wide for the cap
The red day was too small
questions.story: A Kicker triggers and closes strong. The company reports after that same close.
questions.answer: A report was due inside 3 sessions
questions.why: A report was due inside the window. The report came after the Kicker close, and it gapped down next morning. That was GOOGL on 2020-02-03.
questions.lesson_line: The close of the Kicker day was not the end of the risk. Check the calendar.

wrong.The gap was too big to be a Kicker: The gap was not the problem.
wrong.The stop was too wide for the cap: The stop was not the problem.
wrong.The red day was too small: The red day was not the problem.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Take the loss; wait for a new trigger
Move the stop down under the base low
Hold, the base is still intact for now
Buy back at the open
questions.story: Textbook: an 8.1% base, a red day on its low, a 1.7% gap. You bought at 181.81 with the stop at 177.50. Next day it falls through the stop.
questions.answer: Take the loss; wait for a new trigger
questions.why: Take the planned loss. The stop is the exit. This was CDNS on 2021-12-02. A textbook picture, stopped the next day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean chart can still fail. The stop makes the loss small.

wrong.Move the stop down under the base low: A stop never moves down or wider.
wrong.Hold, the base is still intact for now: The stop is the exit. It is not a debate.
wrong.Buy back at the open: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger.

questions.q: What did the stop do?
choices: Its job: a planned loss
Cost you the trade; it needed room
Nothing; the close was the exit
questions.story: You bought at 141.14 with the stop at 137.35. The next day opens at 142.16 and closes at 136.32, under the red high. The stop traded.
questions.why: Its job. The close under the red high was the warning, and the stop traded the same day. That was PGR on 2023-03-16.
questions.lesson_line: The warning came first and the stop did the rest.

wrong.Cost you the trade; it needed room: Giving it room is how a small loss becomes a big one.
wrong.Nothing; the close was the exit: The close under the red high was the warning. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Where does the first stop go?
choices: 41.33, 3.5% under the fill
42.50, under the red high
No stop until the close
Under the red day's low
questions.story: The Kicker opens 0.2% over the red high at 42.83. You are filled at the open and the day has no low yet.
questions.why: 41.33. It opened just over the red high and filled at 42.83, so there is no low yet. The first stop is 3.5% under the fill. That was COHR on 2024-01-16.
questions.lesson_line: An open fill starts at 3.5% under, then follows the 30-minute low.

wrong.42.50, under the red high: The red high is the trigger. The first stop is the 3.5% cap.
wrong.No stop until the close: A real stop is in from the start.
wrong.Under the red day's low: The stop sits under the Kicker day.

questions.q: What did the trims do for you?
choices: Banked two thirds before the give-back
Nothing; the stop took it all
Banked the whole position
Locked in a loss on the whole position
questions.story: You bought a Kicker at 68.80 with the stop at 67.36. It hit 3R on day 1 and 5R soon after, then fell back to your stop at breakeven.
questions.answer: Banked two thirds before the give-back
questions.why: They banked two thirds. ATRO reached 13.8R in two weeks on the scan's fixed stop, then gave most of it back.
questions.lesson_line: Take the thirds as they come. The stop will find the rest.

wrong.Nothing; the stop took it all: The thirds at 3R and 5R were already sold.
wrong.Banked the whole position: Only two thirds were sold; the last third came out at the breakeven stop.
wrong.Locked in a loss on the whole position: Two thirds were sold at a profit, and the stop was lifted to breakeven.

questions.q: Bigalow's rule is to liquidate if the next day gaps back. That is our rule too.
questions.why: False. Bigalow says to liquidate at once on a gap back. We do not: a gap back is not an exit, only the stop is.
questions.lesson_line: Borrowed exits are not ours. Our exit is the stop.

questions.q: Bigalow says a kicker is usually caused by what?
choices: A surprise news item
A planned stock split
A rising 200-day
An opening-range break
questions.why: A surprise news item. Ours is about positioning, and it is rarely an earnings day.
questions.lesson_line: Bigalow says news. We call it positioning.

wrong.A planned stock split: Bigalow names a surprise news item, not a split.
wrong.A rising 200-day: That is a context filter, not a cause.
wrong.An opening-range break: That is an entry method, not a cause.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the red day. Tomorrow it gaps up through this high. Take it or pass?
choices: Take it; weak close at the 21-day
Pass; a baby red candle
Pass; the base is too loose
questions.answer: Take it; weak close at the 21-day
questions.why: Take it. A tight range into the 21-day and 50-day, a red day closing at its low, then a Kicker closing near its high. It finished the day up 8.8%.
questions.lesson_line: Judge the red day first. A weak close at support sets the trap.

wrong.Pass; a baby red candle: The red day fell 1.8% and closed at 2% of its range. That is a real drop.
wrong.Pass; the base is too loose: The base was a tight range of 6.2%.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the red day. Tomorrow it gaps up through this high. Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; the red day is a baby candle
Take it; the base is tight and quiet
Take it; any gap will do the job
questions.answer: Pass; the red day is a baby candle
questions.why: Pass. The red day is a baby red candle, so nobody is trapped. The gap that followed was a plain breakout.
questions.lesson_line: A tiny red body before the gap is a breakout, not a Kicker.

wrong.Take it; the base is tight and quiet: The base was fine, but the red day is a baby red candle.
wrong.Take it; any gap will do the job: The gap needs a real red day under it.

questions.q: Bulkowski found that the strict kicking candle alone is almost random.
questions.why: True. He says it is almost random, so do not guess the breakout direction from the candle alone.
questions.lesson_line: The shape alone is not an edge. Context and the stop carry the trade.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Pass; the gap filled
Buy over the red high
Buy now at half size
Wait for the close
questions.story: An alert says Kicker. At 10:15 the stock traded back to the red close, then bounced and is nearing the red high.
questions.why: Pass. The gap filled before the trigger, so there is no trade. The raw alert fires on gap-filling days.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that fills is a dead Kicker, even if it bounces.

wrong.Buy over the red high: The gap filled before the trigger, so there is no trade.
wrong.Buy now at half size: Half size does not undo a filled gap.
wrong.Wait for the close: The close is never the entry, and the gap already filled.

questions.q: A textbook Kicker chart is enough to take it in any market.
questions.why: False. The pattern alone is not enough. A Red market has none, and a shock-day red bar is not a pullback.
questions.lesson_line: The chart is one filter. The market and the red day are the others.

questions.q: Complete our leader rule.
questions.sentence: We buy leaders with an RS rating of ___ or more.
questions.why: 80. We buy leaders, an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: A Kicker belongs on a leader: an RS rating of 80 or more.

questions.q: Same chart, different business. Which one do you favor?
questions.story: Two leaders show the same clean Kicker: a base, a weak red day, a gap over its high. Stock A has growing sales and earnings. Stock B has flat sales.
choices: Stock A, growth is preferred
Neither, flat sales rule out the trade
Stock B, sales matter more than charts
Skip both until earnings are out
questions.why: Stock A. We prefer growing sales and earnings, but the chart comes first. With matching charts, growth breaks the tie.
questions.lesson_line: Prefer growth, but the chart comes first.

wrong.Neither, flat sales rule out the trade: Growth is preferred, not required. The chart comes first, so flat sales alone do not end the trade.
wrong.Stock B, sales matter more than charts: Backwards. The chart comes first. Growth is the preference when the charts match.
wrong.Skip both until earnings are out: Nothing in the rule asks you to wait for a report. It prefers growth and puts the chart first.

questions.q: Does the base pass our card?
questions.story: A leader's last 20 closes span 12%, so the base looks tidy. Up close, the daily bars inside it are wide and overlap wildly. Yesterday was a weak red day.
choices: Wild, overlapping bars fail it
The 12% span is all that counts
Wide bars show strong demand
It passes at half size
questions.why: It fails. Our card wants no wild, overlapping bars in the base. A tidy 20-close span does not fix a sloppy base.
questions.lesson_line: A tight span is not enough. The bars inside the base must be orderly.

wrong.The 12% span is all that counts: The span is one test. The card also wants no wild, overlapping bars.
wrong.Wide bars show strong demand: Wide, overlapping bars are the sloppy look the card rules out.
wrong.It passes at half size: Size does not fix a failed base. A messy base is a skip.

questions.q: Is there a trade?
questions.story: The red day's high is 50.00 and it closed at 48.00. The Kicker day opens at 48.80, a 1.7% gap. It climbs to 49.70, then fades.
choices: No, it never traded over 50.00
Yes, the 1.7% gap is the trigger
Yes, buy the 49.70 high on the fade
Yes, buy the close, the gap held
questions.why: No. The trigger is the Kicker day trading over the red day's high. A gap alone is not the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: The gap sets the stage. The trade over the red day's high is the trigger.

wrong.Yes, the 1.7% gap is the trigger: The gap is needed, but the trigger is a trade over the red day's high.
wrong.Yes, buy the 49.70 high on the fade: That is under the red high. Chasing a fade is not the trigger.
wrong.Yes, buy the close, the gap held: We never buy the close. And it never traded over the red high.

questions.q: The Kicker triggers on a trade over the red day's high, not just a gap up.
questions.why: True. The Kicker day must trade above the red day's high. That is the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Gap up first, then a trade over the red day's high. That second part is the trigger.

questions.q: A Kicker day ran 40.00 to 44.00 and closed at 43.40. Where in its range did it close, in percent?
questions.why: 85. Close minus low, over the range, times 100. Our card wants the close in the top 20% of the range, so this one reads strong.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over the range. A strong Kicker closes in the top of its range.

questions.q: When you buy the trigger, you already know the Kicker will close strong.
questions.why: False. The strong close is unknown at entry. Our card uses it to read and grade the chart afterward.
questions.lesson_line: You buy the trigger, not the close. The strong close is how the chart is graded afterward.

questions.q: How long is a Kicker on top of its base?
choices: Two daily candles
Three daily candles
One daily candle
Five daily candles
questions.why: Two daily candles. The red day and the Kicker day sit on top of the base.
questions.lesson_line: A Kicker is two daily candles on a base: the red day, then the gap day.

wrong.Three daily candles: Our card counts two: the red day and the Kicker day.
wrong.One daily candle: One candle is a gap day. The Kicker needs the red day before it.
wrong.Five daily candles: Our card counts two on top of the base, not five.

questions.q: The red day opened at 51.00 and closed at 50.00. How big is its body, as a percent of the close?
questions.why: 2. The body is the open minus the close, over the close: 1 on 50. Our card measures the red day's body as a percent of the close.
questions.lesson_line: Body as a percent of the close: open minus close, over the close.

questions.q: What is the best use of tonight?
questions.story: A leader closed a weak red day at support. If it gaps up through the red day's high tomorrow, you want the Kicker. It is 8 pm.
choices: Write down entry, stop and size
Wait and pick the stop after the fill
Set an alert and size it by feel
Plan the entry and size at the open
questions.answer: Write down entry, stop and size
questions.why: Write down the entry, stop and size. Every planned buy has all three on paper before the market opens.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop and size are written before the open. Not after the fill.

wrong.Wait and pick the stop after the fill: The stop is written down before the open too, not picked after the fill.
wrong.Set an alert and size it by feel: An alert is not a plan. The size comes from a written stop.
wrong.Plan the entry and size at the open: The open is too late. All three are written before the market opens.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
questions.story: The red high is 60.00. The Kicker day opens at 59.00 and dips to 58.40. It then trades over 60.00 and you are filled at 60.01.
choices: A few cents under the 58.40 low
Exactly on the 58.40 low so far
3.5% under the 60.01 fill price
The final low, picked at the close
questions.answer: A few cents under the 58.40 low
questions.why: A few cents under 58.40. On our card the low at the fill means the low so far, and that stop is closer than 3.5% under the fill.
questions.lesson_line: At the fill the low is the low so far. You cannot wait for the final low.

wrong.Exactly on the 58.40 low so far: The stop sits a few cents under the low, not exactly on it.
wrong.3.5% under the 60.01 fill price: That is the cap. The stop is the low so far when that is closer.
wrong.The final low, picked at the close: The close is too late. You need the stop with the broker when you buy.

questions.q: With entry B, the low for the stop is the first 30-minute bar's low.
questions.why: True. With entry B the low means the low so far, which is the 30-minute bar's low.
questions.lesson_line: At entry the low is the low so far, not the day's final low.

questions.q: A stop you keep in your head works if you watch the screen closely.
questions.why: False. Every position has a real stop order with the broker. A stop in your head is not a stop.
questions.lesson_line: Put the stop in with the broker the moment you buy.

questions.q: What about the stop?
questions.story: You bought a Kicker at 42.00. After 10:00 the broker stop sits at 41.30. At 1:00 pm the stock is at 41.50 and you feel it will bounce.
choices: Leave it; the stop only moves up
Lower it to 40.50 to give it room
Cancel it and watch the screen
Widen it to 41.00 and wait
questions.answer: Leave it; the stop only moves up
questions.why: Leave it. The stop only moves up, never down or wider. Lowering it turns a planned loss into a bigger one.
questions.lesson_line: A stop only moves up. If you want to lower it, the answer is no.

wrong.Lower it to 40.50 to give it room: That widens the stop. A stop never moves down.
wrong.Cancel it and watch the screen: A stop kept in your head is not a stop. It stays with the broker.
wrong.Widen it to 41.00 and wait: Wider is the same mistake. The stop only moves up.

questions.q: Move the stop up yet?
questions.story: You bought at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. The Kicker is up 1R. A friend says to move the stop to breakeven now.
choices: Not yet; breakeven is 2R to 5R
Yes, breakeven at 1R is the rule
Sell a third now, then breakeven
Yes, trail it under the 10-day
questions.why: Not yet. We move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R. At 1R the original stop stays.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R. At 1R the first stop still stands.

wrong.Yes, breakeven at 1R is the rule: The rule is 2R to 5R. 1R is under that range.
wrong.Sell a third now, then breakeven: The first trim is a third at 3R, not at 1R.
wrong.Yes, trail it under the 10-day: The trail is for the last third, after the trims.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: We move the stop to breakeven between 2R and ___R.
questions.why: 5. Our rule moves the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven window: 2R to 5R.

questions.q: Bought at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 24.22. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add five of those to the fill. The second third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 5R before the open. The second third comes off there.

questions.q: What is next at 24.22?
questions.story: You bought a Kicker at 22.17 with the stop at 21.76. You sold a third at 23.40 and lifted the stop to breakeven. Now it trades at 24.22, which is 5R.
choices: Sell a third more, trail the last
Sell all the rest and bank the 5R
Hold two thirds, skip the 5R trim
Add a third more at the higher price
questions.answer: Sell a third more, trail the last
questions.why: Sell another third, then trail the last third. At 5R the second third comes off.
questions.lesson_line: Third at 3R, third at 5R, then trail the last third.

wrong.Sell all the rest and bank the 5R: The last third is trailed, not sold at 5R.
wrong.Hold two thirds, skip the 5R trim: The rule sells the second third at 5R. It does not skip it.
wrong.Add a third more at the higher price: We buy once, at one price. No adds.

questions.q: Into a burst like this, what fits our rule?
questions.story: You bought a Kicker at 22.17 two weeks ago. It has now risen three days in a row on gaps, each day's range wider than the last, far over its 10-day.
choices: Sell a big part into the burst
Add more, the trend is strong
Hold it all until the 10-day breaks
Sell all of it at the first gap
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the burst
questions.why: Sell a big part. Into a climax run on your own long we sell a big part, and it is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: Climax run on a winner: sell a big part into it.

wrong.Add more, the trend is strong: We buy once. A burst is a time to sell into strength, not to add.
wrong.Hold it all until the 10-day breaks: That gives back the burst. The rule sells a big part into it.
wrong.Sell all of it at the first gap: The rule says a big part, as a judgment call, not everything.

questions.q: A climax run on a winner is a time to sell a big part, not to add.
questions.why: True. Into a climax run on your own long we sell a big part. It is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: Sell a big part into a climax run. Do not add.

Judgment call for the owner: the earnings-day Kicker. The card's kk.not_earnings is pending (D-025). q12 keys only the card's own context line (the Kicker is rarely an earnings day) and the lookalike tell (the first session after a report is graded as an earnings gapper, a PEG), and q48 keys the LUV near-miss on that tell. If the owner picks option c (earnings days allowed when the chart fits), q12 and q48 need a second look.

Textbook or ours: the tested Japanese kicking pattern (Bulkowski, Schwab) is two shadowless candles with a gap between the bodies; none of the kept Kickers on the card passes it. Bigalow's looser Kicker Signal measures the gap from the prior open (q36's wrong note) and exits on a gap back (q64). The unit teaches ours; q10 and q68 use the textbook only to name the difference.
Bigalow says a kicker usually follows a surprise news item (2008). Ours is positioning and 'rarely earnings'. q65 asks what Bigalow says, not what is true for us.

The dossier's example numbers (d1) are read off our own daily bars by the research scan, not a public page: the walk-through fills are the red high plus a cent (BBY 27.97, MS 22.17, ATRO 68.80) or the open when it gapped over it (COHR 42.83). The stop shown with each example is 5 cents under the Kicker day's final low or 3.5% under, whichever is closer; a live trader does not know the final low (kk.stop_low_so_far), so q25, q31 and q62 teach the live version: 3.5% under an open fill, raised at 10:00.
